jobs.title: Senior Water Resources Engineers - Seeking Expressions of Interest
jobs.description:
The importance of water to the health of our world can’t be overstated.

As the frequency and intensity of floods, droughts and storms increases, the water industry must continue to build resiliency and lead from the front.

Together with our clients, we are thinking and doing things differently to help pre-empt and prepare for what's next. Be a part of this dynamic and committed team of diverse water specialists and drive change for your community.

You’ll be able to apply our powerful global network of skills and decades of experience to create positive water outcomes that respect nature and nurture communities.
  
  
**Who are we looking for?**

Whether your expertise lies in flood modelling, hydrology, hydraulic engineering, surface water, catchments, mine water management or water balance modelling, we'd love to hear from you.

We're particularly interested in professionals with strong experience in TUFLOW and/or GoldSim, who are looking to contribute to major infrastructure, mining, water infrastructure, defence, urban development, dams, tailings, environmental and digital disciplines.

You’ll contribute to meaningful work within a supportive culture that values technical excellence, career growth and flexible opportunities across our connected network.

Positions can be based at any GHD office in Australia, and we’re open to discussing preferences for full time and part time.

**Working with an energetic and high performing team, you may be involved in:**

* Hydraulic, hydrologic and water balance models using tools such as TUFLOW and GoldSim.
* Delivering flood studies, floodplain risk management studies, flood impact assessments and development impact assessments.
* Conducting hydrologic and hydraulic assessments in accordance with Australian Rainfall and Runoff (ARR) methodologies.
* Supporting mine water management studies, operational water assessments and strategic water planning projects.
* Analysing complex catchments, water systems and flood behaviours to support informed decision making.
* Collaborating with multidisciplinary teams across water resources, civil engineering, environmental services, mining, dams, tailings and planning.
* Managing projects, maintaining strong client relationships and engaging with key stakeholders to deliver successful outcomes.
* Contributing to proposals, business development activities and the continued growth of our water resources capability.
* Conducting technical reviews and mentoring emerging professionals across the team.
  

**What you will bring to the team:**

* Degree qualifications in Civil Engineering, Environmental Engineering, Water Resources Engineering or a related discipline.
* Approximately 5 to 15 years of relevant consulting, industry or client-side experience.
* Experience in one or more of the following areas:
  + Flood modelling
  + Hydrology
  + Hydraulic engineering
  + Surface water engineering
  + Mine water management
  + Water balance modelling
  + Water resources planning and assessment
* Strong technical capability in one or more of the following:
  + TUFLOW
  + GoldSim
* Experience delivering complex water resources projects across infrastructure, mining, energy, water, defence or urban development sectors.
* Strong communication, stakeholder engagement and client relationship skills.
* Project management experience and a commitment to delivering high-quality outcomes.
* A collaborative mindset and a passion for mentoring and knowledge sharing.
  

**Interested? Apply now with your CV and a Cover Letter.**

GHD is an equal opportunity employer, and we want everyone to be able to fully participate in our recruitment process. We value a diverse workforce and an inclusive culture. We encourage applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples and people of all identities.

GHD embraces hybrid work arrangements to create a work environment focused on well-being, flexibility and productivity where GHD people can thrive, this supports the diverse needs of our workforce while balancing the benefits of remote working with the value of face-to-face collaboration in the office.

We respectfully ask that no agency resumes be presented at this stage.

#LI-PI1

  

**Come together and make a meaningful impact.**

We bring our people together to create something bigger and solve some of the world's most complex problems. Come and experience the power of commitment and see strategy and ideas come to life when you join GHD.

**Let's drive real change.**

**Our Pledge to You**  
At GHD, we don’t just believe in the power of commitment, we live and breathe it every day.

That’s why we pledge to empower our people to make a positive impact. Combining our deep technical expertise with the capabilities of our clients and partners, we respond to some of the most complex challenges facing our planet today.

See where your commitment could take you.
  
That’s the **#PowerOfCommitment**

**Who we are**  
GHD is a global professional services company that leads through engineering, architecture, and construction expertise. We are an employee-owned company with over 11,000 diverse and skilled individuals, across more than 200 offices spanning five continents.
  
The Power of Commitment is our brand promise. It’s what makes us different. We are bound to our stated vision and determination to address humanity’s most urgent needs: to make water, energy and urbanisation sustainable for generations to come.

jobs.title: Director of Risk Assessment
jobs.description:
**Position Summary**

The Director of Risk Assessment will report directly to the General Counsel and play a crucial role in managing and mitigating risks within our long-term care facilities across California. This position requires a highly skilled and experienced professional with a strong background in nursing administration and a deep understanding of state regulations and standards.

**Essential Duties and Responsibilities:**

* Collaborate with the General Counsel to prepare legal analyses of clinical records.
* Conduct comprehensive risk assessments and develop strategies to mitigate potential risks.
* Ensure compliance with California Department of Public Health (CDPH) regulations and standards.
* Oversee and evaluate staffing standards to ensure optimal care and compliance with state requirements.
* Travel to various facilities throughout California to conduct on-site assessments and provide support.
* Understand and apply workers' compensation standards and regulations to minimize liabilities.
* Provide training and guidance to staff on risk management practices and regulatory compliance.

**Qualifications**

* Registered Nurse (RN) or Licensed Nurse (LN) credentials.
* Minimum of 5 years of experience in the long-term care industry.
* Proven experience in nursing administration within California.
* In-depth knowledge of staffing standards and regulations in California.
* Ability to assist General Counsel with legal analysis of clinical records.
* Willingness to travel extensively within California.
* Thorough understanding of workers' compensation standards and CDPH regulations.

**Skills and Competencies**

* Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
* Excellent communication and interpersonal abilities.
* Detail-oriented with a high level of accuracy.
* Ability to work independently and as part of a team.
* Proficient in using relevant software and tools for risk assessment and compliance tracking.

**Working Conditions**

* May encounter frequent interruptions.
* May be involved with residents, family, and government agencies.
* May be requested to work beyond scheduled working hours at times.
* Is subject to call-back during emergency conditions (e.g., severe weather, evacuation, post-disaster, etc.)
* May be subjected to odors, dust, disinfectants, tobacco smoking or air contaminants.
* May be exposed to infectious waste, diseases, conditions, etc., including TB and the AIDS and Hepatitis B
* viruses.
* May be exposed to or handle hazardous chemicals.

**Physical Requirements**

* Must be able to move intermittently throughout the day.
* Working throughout the nursing areas
* Must be able to lift up to 25 pounds, lifting more weight up to 100 pounds requires assistance.
* Ability to read fine print on tablet, progress notes and/or medical labels.

jobs.title: Principal Scientist, Toxicology
jobs.description:
Overview:

**ROLE AT A GLANCE:**  
The Principal Scientist, Toxicology will provide technical support in substantiating the safety of ingredients, formulas and packaging used in Herbalife inner and outer nutrition products in all stages of product lifecycle to support sustainable business growth. The Principal Scientist, Toxicology will work independently to conduct safety evaluation of ingredients, formulations and packaging, prepare appropriate documentation that meets standards and requirements for product safety and regulatory acceptability. This position will work closely with a wide range of regional and corporate teams across organization to ensure safety compliance of Herbalife products worldwide.

In addition, this position is expected to participate in external trade and science-based initiatives pertaining to the safety of product categories relevant to Herbalife business and leverage external partners to advance the science and brand of Herbalife products. The Principal Scientist is a key position in R&D and must inspire and energize employees through advanced knowledge of toxicology, personal leadership, influence, and thorough planning and drive for timely and appropriate results. This position may need to travel globally up to 10% of time.

**HOW YOU’LL MAKE AN IMPACT:**  

* Critically review, validate and summarize scientific evidence for assessing safety of proposed product formulas and materials (including food and dietary ingredients, additives, personal care ingredients, and their constituents) and provide recommendations to address evidence gaps (if any) to support product development and innovation with minimum supervision.
* Develop safety substantiation for Herbalife’s ingredients and finished products, and prepare written technical reports (e.g. risk assessments, safety monographs, etc.) that meet Herbalife internal standards and regulatory acceptability.
* Use published toxicological frameworks and regulatory guidance documents to perform and review hazard, safety and risk assessments to meet applicable regulatory requirements.
* Prepare responses to inquiries regarding the safety of Herbalife’s ingredients and products from regulatory bodies and customers in the local countries where Herbalife products are marketed.
* Lead and provide support in the design, conduct and evaluation of toxicology studies on existing and new ingredients and formulations with training.
* Lead stakeholder in preparation of requisite toxicological requirements for GRAS dossier preparation for North America and Novel Foods applications for Europe.
* Guide and review the development of safety-based specifications for raw materials and finished products, and advisory label statement review process.
* Communicate product and ingredient safety information verbally and in writing to internal customers, including Formulation, Scientific Affairs, Government Affairs, Regulatory Affairs, Quality Assurance, and Post-market Safety Surveillance departments.
* Perform risk assessment and modeling of chemicals using established toxicological databases and tools such as OHAT systematic review, Benchmark Dose Software, Tox21, AOP and QSAR Toolbox under guidance.
* Remain abreast of current risk assessment methodologies and toxicological sciences relevant to Herbalife product categories and communicate emerging topics and potential implications to internal stakeholders.
* Represent Herbalife’s key business interests on trade association task forces, identify and pursue external Key Opinion Leaders for research collaboration opportunities, and support strategic external engagement with scientific and regulatory communities.
* Communicate critical issues to direct manager and other relevant parties in a timely manner, with recommended solutions including timelines and required resources.
* Follows Company policies, processes and procedures, and performs all duties in an honest, ethical and professional manner.
* Additional duties as assigned.

**LEADERSHIP AND SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES:**  

* N/A

Qualifications:

**QUALIFICATIONS FOR SUCCESS:**

**Education**  

* Master or Doctorate Degree in Toxicology, Pharmacology, or related discipline

**Experience**  

* 10 years of experience in toxicology research, nutrient risk assessment, food safety and/or personal care safety assessment areas. Experience gained before or after earning advanced degree will be accepted.
* Proven records of achieving positive results and adding recognized and quantitative value to business
* Successful track record of completing safety-based tasks including product/ingredient reviews
* Has achieved positive results and adding recognized and quantitative corporate value

**Skills/Certifications**  

* A broad knowledge of toxicology and its application to safety evaluation and risk assessment in food, supplements and/or personal care industry
* Working knowledge of toxicity testing methods and applicable regulatory standards
* Good understanding of emerging toxicological tools and risk assessment approaches
* Ability in interpreting, applying and translating complex scientific data (i.e., analytical and toxicological) for practical business use
* Ability to quickly acquire and apply new areas of scientific knowledge and share such information in a clear manner to a variety of stakeholders
* Ability to solve problems in a practical, timely and collaborative manner with adequate attention to detail
* Ability to work under pressure, adapt, navigate and thrive in a dynamic environment with changing priorities, and meet urgent deadlines
* Able to work in a team environment, including cross-functional and multicultural teams
* Solid communication skills, both written and verbal in English in all platforms
* Good project management skills, self-motivated and capable of working autonomously
* Ability to prioritize, plan and execute complex projects including delegating parts to others as needed
* Competent use of MS Office program

Job Description

At GHD, we don’t just believe in the power of commitment, we live and breathe it every day.

That’s why we pledge to empower all of our people to make a positive impact. Combining our deep technical expertise with the capabilities of our clients and partners, we respond to some of the most complex challenges facing our planet today.

See where your commitment could take you.

Our pledge to you

Join GHD

That’s the #PowerOfCommittment

There’s no pledge more important than the one we make to look after our environment, and we’re committed to helping you do exactly that.

Join us as we strive to ensure a sustainable future for our communities and the world we live in.

Become part of our global network of skilled engineers, scientists, auditors, planners and environmental specialists, all working together to leave this world better than we found it.

Are you ready to lead a dynamic team of Emergency Response/Preparedness and environmental professionals in tackling some of the most pressing challenges facing our environment today?

Who are we looking for?

As a Project Manager
at GHD, you will not only mentor and guide the team but also take the reins in environmental emergencies, collaborating closely with clients and agencies to ensure effective response and resolution.

Your role will extend beyond project management to include business development and client expansion activities, where your expertise in environmental engineering, geology, or related fields will shine. With 5+ years of project management experience under your belt, including a proven track record in emergency response, client relationship management, and business development, you'll bring a wealth of knowledge to the table.

From conducting environmental sampling and monitoring to spearheading regional visibility initiatives, your passion for environmental stewardship and problem-solving will drive our success. If you thrive in a fast-paced environment, possess exceptional communication skills, and are committed to making a difference, join us in shaping a sustainable future. Apply today and Join our Emergency Management (GHD FIRST) team.

This opportunity can be based out of the Chicago office.

Who is GHD FIRST:

GHD Fast Incident Response Services Team (GHD FIRST) delivers turnkey, 24/7/365 incident response and management services throughout North America. The GHD FIRST team provides the following core services:

Emergency Preparedness, Planning, and Drills
Environmental/ Remediation Services

Waste Management
Toxicology/ Risk Assessment
Geographic Information Systems (GIS)/ Database

Digital Technology/ Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) Services
Construction/ Construction Management Services
Crisis Communication and Community Engagement
Litigation Support

GHD has more than 100 offices across North America with over 500 staff trained in emergency response and emergency management procedures. Listed below is a management role currently open to grow and further develop the GHD FIRST business sector within GHD.

Working with an energetic and high performing team, this position offers a variety of work and will see you involved in:

Accountable for one or more medium-sized projects of low to moderate complexity with a small- to medium-sized team. Focus on the creation of the project vision and planning documents and manage the implementation, reporting, and performance of the overall project with the expectation of delivering on time, within budget, and to scope.

Document Preparation: Prepare moderately complex documents using a variety of applications for technology devices, such as standard office software. Also responsible for gathering and summarizing data for reports.
Stakeholder Management: Plan and deliver stakeholder engagement activities to develop effective working relationships for projects and to ensure that stakeholder needs and concerns are identified and met.
Personal Capability Building: Develop own capabilities by participating in assessment and development planning activities as well as formal and informal training and coaching; gain or maintain external professional accreditation, where relevant, to improve performance and fulfill personal potential. Maintain an understanding of relevant technology, external regulation, and industry best practices through ongoing education, attending conferences, and reading specialist media.
Continuous Improvement: Contribute to reviewing existing operations in own area of work, and generate new ideas to assist in identifying continuous improvements.
Work Scheduling and Allocation: Assign short-term work schedules to a team of subordinates in order to achieve expectations while following established timelines.
Project Assurance: Conduct assurance reviews within the project, facilitate the delivery of assurance reviews by independent third parties, and take appropriate action to resolve any issues identified, so that senior stakeholders have confidence that the project can deliver according to time, budget, and quality.
Project Scope Definition: Manage the delivery of research, workshops, and other activities to support the specification and agreement of project deliverables.
Project Planning: Produce workstream or project plans, ensuring that all activities are identified, are appropriately organized to deliver project objectives, and comply with the organization's project management framework.
Project Reporting and Review: Draft project review reports and presentations, including key information, commentary, and recommendations, to support the review process and enable stakeholders to evaluate progress and agree on change.

Project Team Management: Lead a small project team; communicate the necessary outcomes and the direction required to achieve them; coordinate team actions on project tasks; request additional team member support when needed; and identify areas of improvement to build the capability of the team through training, coaching, and mentoring.
Requirements Management: Coordinate the identification and elicitation of requirements; conduct analysis of those requirements for completion and alignment; document and manage requirements throughout the life of the project; and coordinate the verification of the end deliverable. Generally done at the level of project phases.

Act as the first point of contact for clients for new emergency projects, with ability to delegate tasks and request support as required from GHD FIRST team.

Bachelor’s degree in Environmental Engineering, Geology, Environmental Science or a related field

Experience

General Experience: Experience enables job holder to deal with the majority of situations and to advise others (Over 3 years to 6 years)
Managerial Experience: Experience of general supervision of more junior colleagues (7 to 12 months)
Experienced in emergency preparedness, air monitoring, environmental assessment/sampling, ICS, SCAT, PHMSA

We are committed to engaging multidisciplinary teams of science, engineering, and regulatory experts to empower our clients with solutions that create a safer, healthier, more sustainable world. For over five decades, we've connected the lessons of past failures with tomorrow's solutions to advise clients as they innovate technologically complex products and processes, ensure the safety and health of their users, and address the challenges of sustainability.   

Join our team of experts with degrees from top programs at over 500 universities and extensive experience spanning a variety of industries. At Exponent, you’ll contribute to the diverse pool of ideas, talents, backgrounds, and experiences that drive our collaborative teamwork and breakthrough insights. Plus, we help you grow your career t hrough collaboration, our rich client network, and our excellent support staff . Thanks for your interest in joining our team!

Key statistics:

640+ Ph.D.s
90+ Disciplines 
30+ Offices globally

Our Opportunity

We are currently seeking a n experienced consultant for a Principal Toxicologist
position in our  Health Sciences  Practice
. This position is open to all U.S. office location s . In this role, you will work as part of a team to provide a high level of leadership and collaboration on projects related to litigation support, toxicological evaluations, risk assessment, and risk communication involving a wide range of products and chemicals . This includes evaluating health hazards, mechanism s of action, dose response, exposure levels , and conducting comparative risk research, utilizing data science tools, assist ing with regulatory documents and analyses , and conducting risk assessments under a variety of regulatory and legal paradigms . As a Principal Toxicologist, you will lead projects, identify new clients, expand relationships with existing clients, develop technical staff, and develop new business in related Health Sciences areas, particularly in the area s of product stewardship, toxic tort, and emerging chemicals of concern. You will be instrumental in helping our clients make and support data-driven and scientifically sound decisions to address today's most pressing issues impacting human health safety.

You will be responsible for

Leverag ing deep knowledge in toxicology to address a wide range of complex human health challenges across diverse client sectors , delivering scientifically rigorous and impactful solutions
Identify ing , pursu ing , and secur ing new client engagements by understanding emerging needs and building long-term partnerships.

Enhance the firm’s visibility and credibility by publishing in peer-reviewed journals, presenting at industry conferences, leading seminars, and participating in expert advisory or technical committees.

PhD in Toxicology or a related scientific field
Minimum of 8 years of consulting experience in the toxicology space
Proven track record of business generation and attracting new and repeat clients or funding

Exceptional verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to articulate complex ideas clearly and persuasively to diverse audiences
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to interpret data, identify trends, and make informed recommendations in your scientific field
Outstanding reputation among clients and the scientific community for integrity, responsiveness, and technical expertise
Adept people management abilities coupled with extensive experience in successfully overseeing and executing complex projects
Strong commitment to professional development 

Applicants are encouraged to submit a CV (Curriculum Vitae) with publications (feel free to include publications that are in review or pending) [not restricted to 1 page].

CARB values diversity at all levels of the organization and is committed to fostering an environment where employees from various backgrounds, cultures, and personal experiences are welcomed and can thrive. CARB offers various modern interview options, including remote phone and video interviews. Join CARB and help us improve the lives of all Californians.

Job Description And Duties

The mission of the Chemical Analysis and Emissions Research Branch is to timely provide accurate measurements of mobile source emissions and fuels and technical expertise to support the California Air Resources Board motor vehicle and clean fuels programs.

The Fuel Analysis and Methods Evaluation Section (FAMES) is looking for an individual with strong work ethics, strong background in analytical chemistry, and good communication skills. The section analyzes motor vehicle fuels at the Southern California Head Quarters (SCHQ) in Riverside. The results are used in determining compliance with the cleaner burning gasoline and clean diesel regulations. FAMES also provides support to the Motor Vehicle Program by analyzing fuels used in emissions testing and providing expertise on the impact of fuel properties on emissions. Full-time, fixed-term opportunity until September 2027

Make a visible difference to public health and community wellbeing

$104,790 - $114,015 per annum (pro rata to apply), plus superannuation and RDOs

Commuter-use, tool-of-trade vehicle provided

Help shape a healthier, safer Boroondara. We’re looking for a motivated, community-minded Environmental Health Officer to join our dedicated team and deliver practical, trusted public health outcomes across the municipality.

About the role

You’ll combine fieldwork, investigation and education to protect public health and support local food and health businesses. Working with an experienced team, you’ll conduct inspections, investigate hazards, guide businesses through legislative requirements and take proportionate action where needed. You’ll also participate in a rotating on-call roster, helping our community remain safe, resilient and well informed.

About you

You’re a qualified Environmental Health professional who brings sound knowledge of public health legislation , confident judgement and a genuine commitment to community wellbeing. You communicate clearly, build constructive relationships and approach complex situations with integrity, empathy and practical problem-solving.

You’ll thrive here if you can balance competing priorities, work collaboratively and deliver excellent customer service in a fast - paced regulatory environment. A commitment to continuous learning and improvement will help you make a strong contribution from day one.

Key responsibilities

Undertake inspections, assess compliance and provide clear, practical guidance to food and public health businesses.

Respond to community health complaints and incidents, investigate risks including food adulteration and infectious disease, and take appropriate education or enforcement action.

Maintain accurate records and prepare high-quality reports, notices and evidence for legal proceedings where required.

Represent Council in legal proceedings when required and contribute to health promotion initiatives.

Support the development of colleagues and students, and improve procedures, registers and systems.

Help strengthen public health service delivery and community safety across Boroondara.

Why join us

At the City of Boroondara, your work has a direct and meaningful impact. You’ll join a collaborative, respectful and forward-thinking organisation where people are empowered to contribute ideas, build their capability and deliver better outcomes for the community.

Benefits

Enjoy flexible work arrangements, generous leave entitlements, wellbeing programs , RDOs and ongoing professional development . You’ll be supported by a collaborative team that values your expertise and gives you the opportunity to do work that matters.

If you want to know more about the of working for the City of Boroondara, please visit our

Bachelor of Applied Science (Environmental Health) or equivalent including eligibility to be a member of Environmental Health Australia.

Conversant with, and able to interpret, all legislation and standards relating to public health.

Applicants must have the right to work in Australia.

Preferred applicants will be required to undergo a National Police Record Check and hold a valid Working with Children Clearance.

59 pm on Friday 16 October 2026.

All applications must be made via the online portal; no applications direct to the hiring manager will be considered. No calls or applications from agencies please.

For any further information please refer to the , or contact Katerina Sioulas - Team Leader Health Services during business hours on 0407 818 480 for a confidential discussion.

We understand that this portal may not meet the needs of people who rely on Assistive Technology or have other diverse requirements. If you have any difficulty using our recruitment system, please do not hesitate to contact People Culture and Development on (03) 9278 4401 or to allow us to help in any way we can.

Who are we?

The City of Boroondara is a metropolitan council, representing more than 170,000 people in the inner-eastern suburbs of Melbourne. A leader in the local government sector, with a reputation for innovation and excellence, we believe in providing an environment where our staff thrive, both in the work they do and in how they learn and develop as people and professionals.

We like to challenge the norm and we are investing significantly in innovation and technology improvements in order to provide our customers with an even greater experience and engagement. We are putting our customers at the forefront of what we do with our organisation wide initiative, Transforming Boroondara Program.

You will be instrumental in driving this change across the organisation using best practice approaches to successfully support us from the now to our desired future state.

With so much going on it’s a great time to join Boroondara!

### **Job Description and Duties**

The mission of the Chemical Analysis and Emissions Research Branch is to timely provide accurate measurements of mobile source emissions and fuels and technical expertise to support the California Air Resources Board (CARB) motor vehicle and clean fuels programs.

  

The Fuel Analysis and Methods Evaluation Section (FAMES) is looking for an individual with strong work ethics, strong background in analytical chemistry, and good communication skills. The section analyzes motor vehicle fuels at the Southern California Head Quarters in Riverside. The results are used in determining compliance with the cleaner burning gasoline and clean diesel regulations. FAMES also provides support to the Motor Vehicle Program by analyzing fuels used in emissions testing and providing expertise on the impact of fuel properties on emissions. Both functions require the evaluation, development, and implementation of more precise and accurate methods of analysis. FAMES is also responsible for proposing the adoption of new and updated methods into California regulations.

  

Under the direction of the FAMES Manager, the Staff Air Pollution Specialist serves as an independent technical expert to oversee fuels analyses and methods. In addition, the incumbent will apply engineering principles to perform the more complex work of evaluating fuel effects on vehicle emissions and develop test methods for the fuel regulations when the need arises. Duties include evaluating and improving fuel analysis test methods; conducting fuel sample analysis; and overseeing the fuel analysis work conducted by other staff, conducting second-level quality control on reported data, reviewing literature studies related to fuel effect issues, and developing test plans to investigate fuel impacts. The incumbent will be responsible for data analysis, interpretation, reports, and oral presentations to stakeholders. The incumbent may also act as an expert witness for CARB or any related court action.

CalRecycle’s Office of Environmental Justice, Tribal Relations, Education and Outreach is seeking a Senior Environmental Scientist (Specialist) to serve as a lead technical expert on environmental justice and tribal-relations issues. The incumbent will conduct advanced scientific analyses, guide departmentwide integration of environmental justice and tribal priorities, and lead complex evaluations of program impacts on California Native American tribes, disadvantaged communities, low-income populations, rural communities, and farmworkers. jobs.title: Environmental Health Program Supervisor
jobs.description:
The Environmental Health Services Division of San Mateo County Health is seeking well-qualified candidates for the position of Environmental Health Program Supervisor.
Program Supervisors, under direction, supervise, direct, organize, manage, evaluate, audit, and provide accountability for one or more Environmental Health programs in the consumer protection (food, water, housing, vector control, land use, pools, solid waste, infectious waste, and cross connections) or hazardous materials/hazardous waste areas.

Currently, there are two regular vacancies in the Environmental Health Services Division's Consumer Protection Food/Pool Programs and Waste Programs. These positions are located in San Mateo, but will travel/drive throughout the county to perform the duties of the job.

The position in the Consumer Protection Food/Pool Program supervises staff that inspect food sold in markets, restaurants, schools, mobile catering facilities, and special events; educate the public and businesses about proper sanitation and food handling; follow-up on complaints and reports of food-borne illness; provide information on food establishment compliance; inspect public recreational water areas such as swimming pools/spas for health and safety compliance; and verify that businesses selling tobacco products have the appropriate permits.

The position in the Waste Programs supervises staff that inspect solid waste operations such as landfills, transfer stations, Post-Closure Landfill Development projects, medical waste generators, body art facilities and practitioners, and massage establishments. This position also supervises household hazardous waste collection operations for residents and small businesses and implements the County ‘s Safe Medicine Disposal Ordinance.

The ideal candidate
is:

Enthusiastic for and dedicated to public service.
Experienced in working for a regulatory agency with a working knowledge of California Retail Food Code (California Health and Safety Code Division 104, Part 7), FDA Standards, California Swimming Pool Code (California Code of Regulations, Title 22 Division 4).
Experienced in working for a Local Enforcement Agency with working knowledge of solid waste regulatory requirements (California Code of Regulations, Title 14 and 27), the Safe Body Art Act (California Health and Safety Code Division 104, Part 15, Chapter 17), the Medical Waste Management Act (California Health and Safety Code, Division 104, Part 14), and County Code for massage establishments, safe medicine disposal and body art. Experienced in directing hazardous waste operations, ensuring compliance with State requirements and incorporating safety practices.
At least three years of experience related to performing inspections, investigations, and research for an environmental health program in a regulatory agency.
Experience in leading and motivating a team.
Approachable and politically astute with a supervisory style that quickly fosters trust, loyalty, respect and commitment from employees.
An experienced REHS with a thorough understanding of the full range of issues, practices and regulations related to consumer protection.
An innovative leader who has collaborated with other agencies with positive outcomes that benefited public health and public education.
Technologically savvy and knowledgeable of electronic field inspection systems and other computer-based technologies utilized by regulatory agencies.
Highly focused and organized, capable of establishing and implementing program budgets.
An excellent problem-solver with superior oral and written communication skills.
A productive team member, willing and able to coordinate closely with other program supervisors to ensure a standard and efficient implementation of programs.

Examples Of Duties

Duties may include, but are not limited to, the following:

Manage, audit, and standardize activities in assigned program area.
Within a team concept, organize and supervise the activities of professional staff.
Participate in the hiring of assigned staff, recommending selection for management approval.
Evaluate employee performance, counsel employees, and effectively recommend initial disciplinary actions and other personnel decisions.
Assist in training and orientation of new personnel.
Evaluate program needs and recommend budget changes and allocations.
Keep current on developments in field of expertise through participation in professional organizations, attending training programs, and reviewing current legislation.
Develop/maintain program guides for assigned program area.
Maintain liaison with federal, state and local officials regarding standards and regulations; serve as advisor to agencies, commissions and other groups on environmental health issues and problems.
Make presentations to city, county, and special district councils/boards, citizen groups, business owners and others on environmental health issues and programs.
Interpret and enforce state and local laws, ordinances, regulations, and codes in areas of environmental health pertaining to assigned program area.
Evaluate workload of personnel and effectiveness of program in assigned area and prepare reports with recommendations for program modifications.
Review proposed legislation; prepare and review administrative and technical reports and studies reports and studies.
Confer with management on significant program issues, needs, conflicts, problems and accomplishments.
Perform other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

Knowledge of:

The environmental health provisions of the California Health and Safety Code, and the rules and regulations of the State Department of Health Services pertaining to environmental health standards and local ordinances.
Public health/environmental health inspection and investigation principles, practices, and administrative procedures.
The principles and techniques of program management.

Skill/Ability to:

Plan, organize and supervise the work of others.
Manage programs in a team environment.
Train others in the principles and techniques of enforcement work.
Define difficult problem areas, analyze complex data and make valid recommendations.
Establish and maintain cooperative working relationships with others.
Speak effectively and make public presentations.
Prepare clear, concise reports and correspondence.

Experience and Education:

Any combination of education and experience that would likely provide the required knowledge, skills and abilities is qualifying. A typical way to qualify is:

Four years increasingly responsible experience as an Environmental Health Specialist or Hazardous Materials Specialist, which includes two years experience in a regulatory agency.

Licensure/Certification:

Possession of a California certificate as a Registered Environmental Health Specialist within two years from date of hire.
Possession and maintenance of a valid Class C California driver license or equivalent.

Application/Examination

jobs.title: Water Agency Environmental Specialist I - Environmental Compliance
jobs.description:
**Position Information**
------------------------


**Sonoma Water is seeing a passionate and driven Environmental Specialist I professional to join our team!**  

**Join us in protecting and enhancing Sonoma County’s natural resources through meaningful, impactful work.**  

  

The Sonoma Water Agency is seeking a qualified candidate to fill a Water Agency Environmental Specialist I position responsible for working on environmental compliance and permitting matters for Sonoma Water projects.


At Sonoma Water, Environmental Specialists are responsible for evaluating, analyzing, and reporting on the environmental impacts of water supply, flood control, sanitation, and sustainability projects. To comply with federal, state, and local regulations, these positions assist in developing and proposing mitigation strategies to avoid, reduce, or offset the environmental impacts of projects. The Environmental Specialist I also uses an interdisciplinary approach from applied knowledge of biology, ecology, environmental science, and hydrology to:  

  

  

* Assist with the preparation of California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) studies, such as categorical exemptions, mitigated negative declarations, environmental impact reports, and technical resource reports
* Assist with preparation of environmental regulatory permit applications to local, state, and federal resource agencies
* Perform field assessments and surveys for sensitive resources, such as aquatic and terrestrial habitat features, wildlife, botanical, and fisheries resources to evaluate environmental effects and determine potential impacts from projects
* Review natural resource studies and reports to understand historical and current site conditions of a project
* Review project information, schedules, studies, and designs, and assist in preparing tracking tools, standard operating procedures, and reports for projects
* Assist in the preparation and review of documents to comply with state, federal, and local environmental laws and regulations; land use planning projects; grant applications; and right\-of\-way activities
* Stay up to date with environmental laws such as the CEQA, National Environmental Protection Act (NEPA), Clean Water Act, Porter\-Cologne Water Quality Control Act, California and Federal Endangered Species Acts

  

The ideal candidate for this position is a team player and passionate about the environment and its resources. They will possess strong communication, problem\-solving, and project organizational skills. In addition, they will possess experience conducting many of the following activities:
* Knowledge of and experience with handling threatened, endangered, and/or sensitive species listed under state or federal endangered species acts (such as California red\-legged frog, California tiger salamander, steelhead trout, and California freshwater shrimp)
* Conducting field assessments and investigations for natural resources such as aquatic and terrestrial habitat features, wildlife and botanical resources in remote areas (e.g. agricultural lands, meadowlands, forests, and aquatic and riparian habitats)
* Collecting, analyzing, and reporting on environmental scientific data associated with natural resources, specifically wildlife
* Researching the historical land uses, existing conditions, and natural resources of a project site, and associated local, state, and federal regulations applicable to the resources and project
* Preparation of CEQA and/or NEPA compliance documents for public projects
* Applying for and acquiring environmental regulatory permits from local, state, and federal resource agencies
* Reviewing the development of public projects (specifically water utility projects) and their associated schedules, studies, and designs
* Collaborating with planners, engineers, contractors, and consultants on the design and construction of public projects (specifically water utility projects)

**Note: This position typically works Monday\-Friday during regular business hours but may be required to work evening, weekend, or holiday shifts to conduct field investigations, help with biological seasonal monitoring, and attend public meetings or community events.**

  

  

**About Sonoma Water**
  

Sonoma Water is a special district formed by the California State Legislature in 1949 and is responsible for providing a safe and reliable water supply to its customers in Sonoma and Marin counties. Sonoma Water also maintains 75 miles of flood control channels and provides sanitation services. Employing approximately 250 employees, Sonoma Water consists of four divisions, including Engineering \& Resource Planning, Environmental Resources, Business Services \& External Affairs, and Water/Wastewater Operations \& Maintenance. Sonoma Water supports the concept of environmental sustainability, focusing on renewable power sources, and strives to be a leader in its water use efficiency and fishery restoration programs.
  

  

Employees of Sonoma Water are employees of a special district and are not subject to the provisions of the Civil Service Ordinance of the County of Sonoma.**What We Offer**


Working at the County of Sonoma offers expansive opportunities for growth and development, the ability to be a part of a challenging and rewarding work environment, and the satisfaction of knowing you're working to better our communities. You can also look forward to flexible work arrangements and excellent benefits\* including:


* **Hybrid Telework** \- A schedule that meets the needs of our staff, department operations, and the communities we serve may be available depending on the assignment
* **Salary Advancement** \- A salary increase after 1,040 hours (6 months when working full\-time) for good work performance; eligibility for a salary increase for good performance every year thereafter, until reaching the top of the salary range
* **Paid Time Off** \- Competitive vacation and sick leave accruals, 12 paid holidays

Ramboll is a global architecture, engineering, and consultancy company. As a foundation-owned people company, founded in Denmark, we believe that the purpose of sustainable change is to create a thriving world for both nature and people. So, that’s where we start – and how we work. Our history is rooted in a clear vision of how a responsible company should act and being open and curious is a cornerstone of our culture. Ramboll experts deliver innovative solutions across Environment & Health, Water, Energy, and Planning & Urban Design.

Job Description

Applicants must be currently authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis. No sponsorship is available for this position.

Are you eager to develop your technical and professional excellence and advance your career in a collaborative, inclusive, diverse, and empowering culture? Ramboll is a leading scientific and environmental consulting firm providing a broad range of technical services to both public and private sector clients. When you join Ramboll, you will become part of a company that strives to make a difference – for our employees, clients, and society.

Ramboll is seeking an entry-level to mid-level consultant to join the Risk Assessment and Community Health group in one of the firm’s Oakland, CA office. Hybrid work arrangements are available, with office presence required at least two days a week.

Your new role

As an entry-level health sciences consultant at Ramboll, you will support a range of human health risk assessment and community health projects in a collaborative, fast-paced environment. Your work will include independent, detail-oriented technical tasks as well as coordination with colleagues and project teams. Projects may be related to hazardous waste and other contaminated sites, Brownfield redevelopment, vapor intrusion, ambient and indoor air quality, product safety, regulatory interactions, community engagement, and litigation. Tasks may include data management, statistical analysis, fate and transport modeling, spatial analysis, sampling/remediation/risk management planning, and technical reporting. This is a unique opportunity to work with Ramboll experts to advance your technical and consulting skills.

Your key responsibilities will be:

Compiling, organizing, and managing environmental data and databases; performing statistical and geospatial analyses of environmental and health data.
Evaluating the environmental fate and transport of chemicals
Estimating human exposures to chemicals in different environmental media (e.g., air, soil, sediment, fish tissue, produce, water, etc.) and exposure scenarios, and calculating associated health risks.
Assisting with preparation of technical reports, written communication, proposals, and presentations
Reviewing and evaluating technical documents (e.g., scientific articles, regulations)

Qualifications

Advanced degree (M.S., MPH or equivalent) in Environmental Science or Engineering, Environmental Health Science and/or Environmental Toxicology
Exemplary individuals with bachelor’s degree and 2 + years of relevant experience may be considered.

2+ years of chemistry coursework required.
Current authorization to work in the United States on a full-time basis, where required for the position.

Knowledge of risk assessment, exposure assessment, and fate and transport of chemicals in the environment
Proficiency with MS Office; experience with MS Access or other relational databases (e.g., SQL) for managing, querying, and analyzing environmental data.
Demonstrated strong quantitative and problem-solving skills; experienced with statistical and data analysis using R, Python, SQL, or SAS
GIS capability is a plus.
Experience reviewing and evaluating technical documents, scientific articles, regulations, and regulatory guidance.

Meaningful, high-impact work
Flexible and hybrid work arrangements
Competitive compensation and benefits
Professional development and leadership opportunities
A collaborative and inclusive culture
The long-term thinking of a foundation-owned company

Hybrid role based between the office and the field; ability to travel 2–5 days a week (transportation provided or compensated). Monday–Friday schedule; occasional weekend work may be required.

Field Operations & Installation

Conduct onsite installation, startup, and commissioning of meteorological and ambient air quality monitoring equipment.
Draw upon hands-on technical experience to perform analyzer maintenance, troubleshooting, and calibrations at remote monitoring sites, minimizing downtime and data loss.

Apply practical field experience to support the design, integration, and build-out of ambient air quality monitoring systems.

Quality Assurance & Compliance

Maintain current audit and calibration certifications, and apply working knowledge of EPA and state monitoring protocols in the field.
Provide QA of air quality audit and calibration reports.
Review incoming data with an experienced eye to proactively flag instrumentation issues before they affect data quality.
Provide proper documentation and record keeping for all air quality systems and network servicing and auditing.

Client & Program Support

Provide meteorological sensor and air quality instrument calibration, maintenance, and audit services for numerous clients across the U.S., with a concentration in California.

Qualifications

4–8+ years of hands-on field experience in ambient air quality or meteorological monitoring; a Bachelor’s degree in environmental science, meteorology, or engineering may be considered in place of equivalent field experience.

Required Skills

Demonstrated, practical experience with DC electronics, telemetry, and remote data logging equipment.
Working knowledge of state and Federal (EPA) environmental monitoring guidelines and regulations, gained through direct application at active monitoring sites.
Hands-on mechanical and electrical troubleshooting experience.
Strong work ethic, attention to detail, and proven problem-solving skills; comfortable working independently and as part of a team.

Proven, hands-on experience operating and maintaining meteorological and air quality instrumentation.

##### **About Peraton**


Peraton is a next\-generation national security company that drives missions of consequence spanning the globe and extending to the farthest reaches of the galaxy. As the world’s leading mission capability integrator and transformative enterprise IT provider, we deliver trusted, highly differentiated solutions and technologies to protect our nation and allies. Peraton operates at the critical nexus between traditional and nontraditional threats across all domains: land, sea, space, air, and cyberspace. The company serves as a valued partner to essential government agencies and supports every branch of the U.S. armed forces. Each day, our employees solve the most daunting challenges that our customers face. Visit peraton.com to learn how we’re keeping people around the world safe and secure.


##### **Program Overview**


Provide critical communications and tracking for multiple spacecraft from three complexes located globally, and operates year round 24 hours/7days to provide continuous contact with the spacecraft. The program fulfills NASA goals by supporting NASA deep space mission set, including NASA\-funded missions and collaborative international missions.
##### **About The Role**


Peraton is seeking an **Environmental Analyst** to support our Deep Space Network (DSN) Operations and Maintenance contract with NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory in Fort Irwin, CA.

  

The Deep Space Network is NASA’s international array of giant radio antennas that supports interplanetary spacecraft missions, plus a few that orbit Earth. The DSN also provides radar and radio astronomy observations that improve our understanding of the solar system and the larger universe. The antennas of the Deep Space Network are the indispensable link to explorers venturing beyond the moon. They provide the crucial connection for commanding our spacecraft and receiving their never\-before\-seen images and scientific information on Earth, propelling our understanding of the universe, our solar system and ultimately, our place within it.

  

**Responsibilities:**

  

The Environmental Analyst supports and manages environmental compliance programs, regulatory reporting, data analysis, inspections, and permitting. The role requires the ability to interpret federal, state, and local environmental regulations and translate them into practical compliance programs, working closely with EHS, operations, engineering, facilities, maintenance, and management.

Are you looking to make a difference and join a highly motivated team working on issues critical to ensuring the safety and sustainability of California? The Office of Energy Infrastructure Safety's Environmental Science Division is seeking a Senior Environmental Scientist Specialist to analyze performance with vegetation management commitments in electrical utility Wildfire Mitigation Plans (WMP).  

  

  

The Environmental Science Division is responsible for evaluating the vegetation management aspects of utility WMPs, assessing performance in meeting vegetation management\-related commitments described in the WMPs, and ensuring that each utility is reducing its risk of igniting a catastrophic wildfire. To this end, Division scientists review regulatory filings and utility procedures, analyze reported data, perform audits, conduct field inspections, publish findings, and engage with the utilities and interested parties. Division scientists serve as subject\-matter experts in utility vegetation management and environmental policy related to wildfire risk reduction. Our team of scientists is highly collaborative and works closely with the Performance Assessment, Electric Safety Policy, and Data Analytics Divisions.  

  

  

Under general direction of the Senior Environmental Scientist Supervisor of the Inspections \& Investigations Branch the incumbent will lead inspections of vegetation near electrical infrastructure, write and review inspection reports, lead development of inspection plans to assess electrical corporation performance with approved Wildfire Mitigation Plans (WMPs) and other regulatory requirements of the Department associated with forestry, wildfire science, and the environment. Incumbent will also lead investigations into concerns raised by external parties and other potential WMP deficiencies, conduct critical and/or sensitive scientific investigations and studies and prepare guidance, policy, planning, or regulatory documents and legislative proposals on issues of importance to the department. Incumbent will identify issues found in the field and elevate to the Supervisor with proposed recommendations. The incumbent will provide guidance to and assist the branch Environmental Scientists with document reviews and deliverables prior to submittal to management. The incumbent will develop and maintain positive relationships with internal and external agency partners. The incumbent will be the subject matter expert on vegetation management programs to assess electrical utility performance with approved WMPs and other regulatory requirements of the Department associated with forestry, wildfire science, climate change and the environment.

Optus is an Australian telecommunications company, delivering more than 11 million services to our customers every day across mobile, broadband, and digital solutions.

  

As the Remediation Team Leader at Optus, you'll play a critical leadership role within our customer division. In this role, you will lead a team responsible for resolving the most complex, high\-risk, and high\-impact customer issues. jobs.description:
Water Quality & Remote Sensing Research Scientist

University Corporation at Monterey Bay

Salary: $108,000.00 – $126,000.00 Annually

Job Number: 2026-00030

Location: Various Field Locations (see posting)

Department: Applied Environmental Science

Description

Water Quality & Remote Sensing Research Scientist

ARC CREST

NASA Ames Research Center / CSUMB Dept of Applied Environmental Science

Job Announcement

Priority Screening Deadline: October 5, 2026. All positions are open until filled.

This position is dependent upon grant funds. Subject to annual NASA review

Position December 1, 2026 through December 31, 2027.

SALARY

Salary Grade: Staff, Grade 6

Hiring Range: $108,000 – $126,000 annually

The University Corporation is committed to providing our employees with a comprehensive program that rewards efforts that are appreciated by colleagues, students, and the customers we serve. Salary placement is determined by the education, experience, and qualifications the candidate brings to the position, internal equity, and the hiring department’s fiscal resources. Our salary schedule is available https://csumb.edu/departments/corporation/policies/.

Benefits Summary

The University Corporation provides a comprehensive benefits package, which includes:

–

Medical, dental, and vision insurance

–

Life and disability insurance

–

Retirement plan with employer contributions

–

Voluntary 403(b) savings plan

–

Generous vacation and sick leave accruals

–

Paid holidays

–

Access to campus dining plans

–

Eligibility for affordable campus housing (if applicable)

Applicants are encouraged to review additional benefit information below for full details.

Position Summary

Under the general direction of the Principal Investigator under the NASA ARC-CREST Cooperative Agreement, the Research Scientist is responsible for conducting scientific research, publishing scientific papers, and developing proposals for new research activities. Additionally, the Research Scientist will serve as a water quality and remote sensing subject matter expert and contribute to NASA capacity building efforts with the Applied Remote Sensing Training (ARSET) program.

The main objectives of this research are validation and advancement of satellite-based water quality and cyanobacterial harmful algal bloom monitoring tools that utilize NASA Earth observation data including hyperspectral imagery. Work under this position includes in situ water quality and optical data collection for remote sensing validation, image processing, atmospheric correction, data analysis, and water quality solutions development.

The candidate will need to be capable of both working independently and collaborating within a team environment on tasks performed across a spectrum of disciplines. The candidate needs to have excellent writing and oral presentation skills. This position will work closely with scientists at NASA Ames Research Center. The successful candidate will have the opportunity and support to develop and lead innovative research on remote sensing of water quality.

Examples of Duties

Key Responsibilities

–

Assist In All Portions Of Content Creation And Delivery Of Online NASA ARSET Trainings For The Water Quality Applications Area Including

–

Conduct background research for training topics.

–

Create and review training presentations.

–

Assist with content creation for training promotion in collaboration with the ARSET communications lead.

–

Assist with participant questions via email and during the training sessions.

–

Contribute to creation of post-training surveys and review of results.

–

Conduct research on application of NASA Earth observations to water quality solutions.

–

Complete water quality and remote sensing validation field work on inland waters.

–

Analyze complex spatial and temporal water quality datasets.

–

Present research results and scientific meetings and to partners and stakeholders at workshops and meetings.

–

Author peer-reviewed scientific manuscripts, research and technical reports, and research proposals.

–

Foster and maintain collaborative links with federal, state, and local agencies in addition to local groups and individuals, research organizations, and the public.

Qualifications

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

Education And Experience

–

Doctoral degree or the equivalent in Civil and Environmental Engineering, Water Resources Engineering, Hydrology, Environmental Science, or a closely related field.

–

Previous Experience With The Following

–

Publication of scientific manuscripts

–

Conducting research or applied science projects with NASA EO data

–

Development of research projects and proposals

–

The ability to access, analyze, visualize data products of NASA EO datasets

–

Experience with public speaking and presentation of scientific results to a variety of audiences.

Preferred Qualifications

–

Familiarity with NASA policies and procedures, and government regulations.

–

Expertise in NASA remote sensing science across multiple sensors and projects.

–

Technical knowledge evidenced by peer-reviewed publications and conferences presentations record on subjects dealing with water quality and remote sensing science utilizing NASA Earth observations.

–

Water quality engineering experience as demonstrated by previous work experience and procession of a Professional Engineering license.

–

Demonstrated understanding of and commitment to the CSUMB Vision Statement and the core values of mutual respect, collaboration and service orientation, multiculturalism and diversity, community service and institutional excellence.

Special Conditions of Employment

SPECIAL CONDITIONS OF EMPLOYMENT

Special License Or Certifications And Conditions

–

Ability to safely operate a motorboat as evidenced by completion of a Motorboat Operator Training Course and possession of a California Boater Card.

–

This position is dependent upon grant funds. Subject to annual NASA review.

–

Position December 1, 2026 through December 31, 2027.

–

May require occasional evenings and/or weekend work.

This position is designated as a mandated reporter under the California Child Abuse and Neglect Reporting Act and must comply with applicable CSU Executive Orders, including Title IX reporting requirements. Employment is contingent upon successful completion of a background check in accordance with the California Fair Chance Act. The University Corporation at Monterey Bay is an equal opportunity employer committed to a diverse and inclusive workplace and complies with all applicable federal and state nondiscrimination laws. University Corporation employment is separate from CSU Monterey Bay and the State of California. All employees must be eligible to work in the United States. Positions are at-will. CSUMB is a smoke and tobacco-free campus.

Additional Benefits Information

The Corporation offers a rich benefits package that constitutes a major portion of total compensation. Benefits include medical, dental, vision, and life insurance benefits, contributory retirement plan, TSA (403b), and more. Please review our https://csumb.edu/departments/corporation/human-resources/employee-benefits/ for details about sick time, vacation, and holidays.

The Corporation also offers access to CSUMB’s Faculty & Staff Meal Plans, which provide convenience, value, and flexibility with our all-you-care-to-eat dining commons, showcasing eight brand new dining concepts for an affordable price.

The University Corporation at Monterey Bay also provides access to affordable campus housing: https://csumb.edu/departments/corporation/services/employee-housing/

Although CSUMB is located in a high-cost housing area, Schoonover Park rental homes are affordably priced. Monthly rent rates include cable television, garbage service, and sewer. Convenient floorplans, attractive interior appointments, and numerous community amenities make Schoonover Park Rental Homes an exceptional value. Schoonover Park is near the main campus, yet a tranquil world away. The community lies nestled in the secluded beauty of rolling coastal hills three miles east of campus. Living in one of the most desirable areas of California, you will enjoy the natural splendor and cultural abundance of the Monterey Peninsula. Quality of life begins with your home in Schoonover Park and extends through every aspect of your California coastal lifestyle. https://www.schoonoverparkapartments.com

About The Corporation

The University Corporation at Monterey Bay (“Corporation”): The Corporation is constantly looking for motivated employees with great organization and teamwork skills to join our team. The Corporation is a non-profit institution that is related to and affiliated with the California State University, Monterey Bay. The University Corporation at Monterey Bay is a nonprofit 501(c)(3) public benefits corporation that is a recognized auxiliary organization of California State University and was established in July 1994. The University Corporation’s mission is to further the educational purposes of the University.

The University: California State University, Monterey Bay is a mid-sized university in California’s Central Coast that grants undergraduate and graduate degrees. Powered by an inspiring Founding Vision Statement, CSUMB is part of the nation’s largest four-year public university system, California State University, which educates nearly 460,000 students every year. With a vibrant, diverse student body of over 7,000 students, CSU Monterey Bay is both a Minority Serving Institution and a Hispanic Serving Institution. Our staff and faculty transform students’ lives with a focus on student success and engagement through experiential learning, service learning, and a strong emphasis on multicultural and global perspectives. CSUMB’s sustainability goal is to be carbon neutral by 2030.

The Community: Monterey, with its moderate Mediterranean climate, is a diverse community on the picturesque central coast of California and rich in agriculture. Miles of beautiful beaches, spectacular mountain ranges, groves of redwoods, low-rolling foothills, and scenic valleys are characteristics that contribute to the quality of life enjoyed by over 432,000 residents and millions of visitors. Boasting such world-renowned attractions as the spectacular Big Sur Coast, Laguna Seca Raceway, 17-Mile Drive, Monterey Bay Aquarium, Cannery Row, the Steinbeck Center, the Monterey Jazz and Blues Festivals and Pebble Beach – possibly the world’s most famous golf course, it’s easy to see why so many choose to live here and an estimated four million visitors a year make the County of Monterey their destination of choice.

How To Apply

All prospective applicants must apply online. The entire application must be completed for submission. We accept applications only for the positions that are currently open and listed on our site. All positions are open until filled. Please do not fax or mail in a printed version of electronic applications, or a resume in lieu of an application. If you are having difficulty applying or need assistance, please call (831)582-3389. The completed online application and resume must be submitted by 5:00 PM PST on the Priority Screening Date to be considered for initial review. Applications received after the Priority Date will be reviewed at the discretion of the Corporation.

AI Disclaimer: University Corporation does not use artificial intelligence or automated decision-making tools to evaluate candidates. All employment decisions are made by human reviewers. Candidates are expected to complete all interviews and assessments independently. The use of AI tools, automated response systems, or other external assistance during interviews or assessments is not permitted and may result in disqualification.

To apply, please visit https://apptrkr.com/9843725

OC San is currently looking to fill the role of an **Environmental Specialist (Quality Assurance/Sampling).**  

  

Under general supervision, performs a variety of professional, technical, and analytical duties and responsibilities in support of OC San’s environmental protection, monitoring, and compliance programs such as conducting routine to moderately complex environmental analyses and studies, collecting and analyzing wastewater, marine, air, ocean sediment, fish tissue, and industrial waste samples, and conducting field work; troubleshoots and repairs equipment and instrumentation; assists in preparing, compiling, and analyzing data for the generation, submission, and distribution of reports and related documentation; and performs duties as assigned.  

  

**Job duties for the Environmental Specialist with the Quality Assurance/Sampling group may include, but not limited to:**
Performs routine and moderately complex fieldwork for sampling efforts; learns to set up, operate, calibrate, maintain, and troubleshoot sampling and monitoring equipment and instrumentation; collects, organizes, prepares, and analyzes a wide variety of samples for operational process control, permit compliance, pretreatment program support, and regional or special projects and studies; receives and/or preserves samples and documents in sample preservation log and in Laboratory Information Management System (LIMS) database. Performs regular and preventative maintenance on basic equipment and instruments; cleans and prepares glassware; maintains quality assurance logs for equipment; performs sampling and sampler support and other lab support duties as needed.


Perform routine and moderately complex QA/QC work. Supports and coordinates contract lab shipping, ordering, and initial data review for routine testing and special projects. Supports document control, management of training records. Participates in LIMS support work. Performs various support equipment QA work, including high purity water and deionized water system. Supports implementation of Proficiency Evaluation (PE) and Proficiency Testing (PT) work, internal and external audits. Participates in QA consultation to lab bench groups. Support client services such as sample receiving and sampling kits preparation for internal clients. Learns to analyze and provide data for the preparation and review of designated sections of the annual report to ensure accuracy. Performs other QA, LIMS, and client service duties as needed.

$85,000+ Super + Paid Overtime / TOIL

Around 2 Days Fieldwork Per Week – Mostly Sydney & Surrounds

Clear Progression into Project Ownership & PM-Level Responsibility

As an Environmental Scientist in Contaminated Land, this is a good time to join a young consultancy that has moved beyond the start-up phase and is now winning the sort of larger projects that create genuine room for people to grow with it.
They don't need another graduate, and they don't need a finished Project Manager. They need the person in between.
Someone with around 2–3 years' consulting experience who understands PSI/DSI work, can handle themselves in the field, writes a decent report and is ready to start taking greater ownership, while still having experienced PMs around them to review, guide and teach.
The business is currently tendering for larger infrastructure and contaminated land projects, while already delivering substantial investigations across industrial sites, renewables and commercial developments. As that pipeline grows, so should your role.

The Role

You'll sit between the junior field team and senior PMs, combining hands-on investigation work with reporting and gradually increasing project responsibility.

You'll:
Deliver PSI, DSI, validation and Acid Sulfate Soil investigations.
Undertake soil and groundwater sampling and broader environmental field investigations.
Work on larger contaminated land programs rather than being stuck doing endless small one-off jobs.
Contribute to investigations involving soil, groundwater, vapour and surface water.
Write PSI/DSI reports, with senior review and technical support available.
Gain exposure to RAPs and waste classifications where projects require it.
Gradually take ownership of defined pieces of work and smaller projects as your capability develops.
Spend around two days per week in the field, occasionally three depending on the project.

Current and recent work includes a 5-hectare industrial DSI covering soil, groundwater, vapour and surface water, a major renewable energy project moving into remediation, larger PSI/DSI programs and further infrastructure projects currently being tendered.
Most fieldwork is around Sydney and surrounding areas. Some sites can mean roughly two hours' travel each way, but there isn't an expectation of constant regional or overnight travel. Where practical, you can travel directly from home to site.

The Team

This is a small, growing consultancy where your contribution will be visible.
You'll have experienced contaminated land people above you for technical support, alongside junior consultants who are earlier in their careers. That puts you in a useful position: experienced enough to get on with the work, but with plenty of room to keep learning.
They're looking for someone independent without pretending you should know everything already. Take a brief, have a crack, research what you don't know and ask sensible questions when you need to.
The business backs that up with professional development, industry training and support toward relevant accreditations and memberships.
Hybrid working is available, along with company vehicles, fuel cards, full PPE, field equipment, laptop and phone. Overtime is paid and TOIL is available, with no regular weekend-work expectation.

Experience

Around 2–3 years' environmental consulting experience, predominantly in contaminated land.
Practical PSI/DSI, soil sampling, environmental investigation and reporting experience.
Some groundwater knowledge plus exposure to Acid Sulfate Soils and validation work.
Most importantly, enough initiative to take ownership of your work while still being comfortable learning from experienced PMs.

This isn't a PM job dressed up as a Scientist role. It's the step before it, with the project exposure and support to help you get there.

Salary starts from $85,000 + super, with paid overtime / TOIL available.
